Night Shift: The Seat Across
Six months of 3 AM coffee across one table. Tomorrow, he works days.
A night nurse and the hospital's logistics coordinator have only ever met exhausted. Now one moves to days, and they have to find out who they are awake.

For six months, Rowan has bought two coffees at 3 AM and Elijah has sat across from him in the basement cafeteria of Eastbrook General. Then Rowan gets moved to days, and the only time they've ever had is gone. Breakfast after the last handoff should be easy — except the floor runs long, 'soon' isn't a time, and somebody ends up waiting on a park bench with a second sandwich. You decide what Rowan asks for, how long he waits, and whether he keeps saving the seat across.
A night-shift coworker who has watched Rowan buy two coffees every night since March and has opinions about it.
If nobody names a real time, the seat across stays empty — and waiting becomes a job only one of them does.

One Coffee
Tell him about the transfer — and leave a door open
Hospital cafeteria, basement level
Wednesday, 3:10 AM
The basement cafeteria at 3 AM: one cashier, one humming fridge, and the table by the vending machine that's been theirs since March.
I set down one coffee. Just mine. I've bought two every night for six months, and my hand still reaches for the second cup.
I sit across from him and look at the empty spot where my coffee always goes.
They ran out?
No. They moved me to days.
When?
Tomorrow. One more night, then I'm a morning person. Allegedly.
Six months of three AM, and I have never once seen him in sunlight.
An elevator dings down the hall. Nobody gets off. The fridge keeps humming like it has opinions.
What does Rowan say next?
Invite him to see you in daylight.

I'll be asleep for most of it. But yes. Give me a day to figure out how.
